summary.intent: Run the full autonomous ship-phase pipeline for GSD phase 73 (verify → secure → validate → simplify → SDK E2E gate → CodeRabbit CLI → ship → resolve PR reviews) without babysitting, applying the three-way fix/todo/discard triage rule to every finding.
summary.outcome: Phase 73 shipped as PR #603 with all pre-ship gates passing (verify 7/7, secure 17/17, validate 0 gaps, SDK E2E 106/106, CodeRabbit CLI 0 findings after fixes) and CI green; PR-level review triage was in progress at transcript end, with one more real fix (seq-consistency guard in client.ts) staged for commit and two todos logged to the existing 68.2 hardening backlog.

repo: Local dev stack: TEE_WORKER_URL defaults to http://localhost:3001, but when mock-ipns-routing already owns host :3001, docker remaps tee-worker to host :3002 — causes silent 404 at API boot and empty tee_key_state table

tee_key_state is populated by the API's TeeService fetching the worker's pubkey at startup (not by the worker itself); worker endpoints are gated by Authorization: Bearer $TEE_WORKER_SECRET (apps/tee-worker/src/middleware/auth.ts)

Phase 73 commit subjects were already conventional (fix(73-08): style, not the problematic feat 73-08: style) — the filter-branch reword step (Step 7) was unnecessary this time; only chore:/docs: merge summaries had parens, which don't drive release-please versioning
CodeRabbit CLI sometimes hallucinates cross-refs to nonexistent phase numbers in .planning/ doc-metadata nits — treat as review noise

resolveIpnsRecord maps 404→null but lets 410 fall through to throw; createAndPublishIpnsRecord was changed in phase 73 (SC4) to catch 410 and return {success:false, tombstoned:true} instead of throwing
.planning/todos/pending/2026-07-06-68.2-coderabbit-hardening-backlog.md is the standing shared-nav hardening backlog — check it for dedupe before filing new shared-nav/write-key todos

code.finding: refreshCurrentDepthWriteKey reseeded publishedNode from cached getSharedFolderState() (stale on tombstone scenario); fixed to call getSdkClient().refreshSharedFolder(currentShareId) first, mirroring the restoreToBreadcrumbIndex pattern (line ~608)
Greptile-flagged in-flight descent race (fast navigate-up during descent seed) is a genuine async TOCTOU but pre-existing nav-architecture issue; deferred as todo rather than fixed at ship time

publishedParent resolve bypassed the seq-consistency check applied to sibling reads; adopting children/seq from one resolve but publishedNode from another with no consistency guard could seed a stale envelope — fixed with a guard mirroring doReresolveFolderInPlace
Test 20 (WRITE-04) asserted the old throw-on-410 contract; updated to assert the new {tombstoned:true} return contract after confirming no production caller relied on the old throw behavior

workflow: Run independent gate agents/checks (secure, crypto/privacy, general security sweep, Nyquist validation, SDK E2E, CodeRabbit CLI) concurrently in the background, then adversarially re-verify their findings by reading the actual source before triaging

Piped bash exit codes can mask real failures (SDK E2E run looked like exit 0 via a task-notification summary but was actually exit 1 due to the pipe) — always tail/inspect actual output, don't trust the notification alone

When an E2E infra failure looks like a missing service, verify container health first, then trace config wiring (port mapping, env defaults, auth secrets) methodically rather than assuming rebuild/restart will fix it
Before filing a new todo, search existing pending todos for a related item and append/refine in place rather than creating a duplicate file

friction: SDK E2E suite's exit code was masked by a pipe, initially appearing to pass (exit 0) when it actually failed (exit 1) with 3 failures

3 SDK E2E failures traced to a two-layer local-stack wiring gap: TEE_WORKER_URL port collision (:3001 vs :3002) plus a TEE_WORKER_SECRET auth mismatch — required deep multi-step diagnosis (container status, DB state, API boot logs, direct port probing) before confirming it wasn't a phase regression

Test 20 (WRITE-04) had a stale assertion left over from before phase 73's throw→return contract change, requiring careful verification that no production caller depended on the old throw behavior before updating the test
Transient network timeout when checking for an existing PR via gh
PR-level review triage required manually mapping GraphQL reviewThreads across two reviewers (CodeRabbit inline findings + Greptile) since neither is filtered by author
